title: Special Reaction Team (SRT) Member (GySgt to Cpl) NMOS (5811), DC I&L
raw_text:
6. MOS 5816, Special Reaction Team (SRT) Member (GySgt to Cpl) NMOS (5811),
DC I&L

    a. Summary. Special Reaction Team Members are Military Policeman
trained to counter and/or contain a high-risk incident surpassing normal law
enforcement capabilities. Members are trained on enhanced marksmanship,
tactical movement, entry, breaching, and clearing objectives in order to
neutralize threats.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a volunteer.

            (2) Possess a high degree of maturity and self-control.

            (3) Must have obtained the grade of corporal or higher.

            (4) Maintain minimum first class physical fitness standards.

            (5) Qualify as and maintain an expert with service rifle and pistol.



                                          3-332                        Enclosure (1)
 3136                                                                 NAVMC 1200.1L



            (6) Must currently hold and maintain all prerequisites of PMOS 5811.

    c. Requirements. Complete the Special Reaction Team Course (Phase I)
(A16MRX3), U.S. Army Military Police School, Ft Leonard Wood, MO or
completion of the Marine Corps Police Academy (MCPA) SRT Phase I Training.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (ac), Military Police, Investigations, and Corrections Training and
Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Police and Sheriff's Patrol Course 33-3051.

    f. Related Military Skill. Marine Corps Security Force (MCSF) Close
Quarters Battle (CQB) Team Member, 8154.

CORRECTIONS 1. Introduction. The Military Police, Investigations, and Corrections OccFld provides the installation commander continuous support by enforcing the law, preventing and suppressing crime, assessing command physical security posture, preserving military control, quelling disturbances, investigating offenses, apprehending offenders, protecting property and personnel, investigating traffic accidents, controlling traffic, providing first response to active shooters incidents and special response to a barricaded subject, guarding military prisoners and supervising brig operations and correctional custody units. Provide the MARFORRES Commander support to security and mobility operations, battlefield circulation and traffic control, rear area security operations to include limited offensive and defensive combat operations, detention operations to include handling and safeguarding prisoners of war, refugees, or evacuees, guarding military prisoners, and returning absentees/deserters to military control.

6. MOS 5816, Special Reaction Team (SRT) Member (GySgt to Cpl) NMOS (5811), DC I&L a. Summary. Special Reaction Team Members are Military Policeman trained to counter and/or contain a high-risk incident surpassing normal law enforcement capabilities. Members are trained on enhanced marksmanship, tactical movement, entry, breaching, and clearing objectives in order to neutralize threats. b. Prerequisites (1) Must be a volunteer. (2) Possess a high degree of maturity and self-control. (3) Must have obtained the grade of corporal or higher. (4) Maintain minimum first class physical fitness standards. (5) Qualify as and maintain an expert with service rifle and pistol. (6) Must currently hold and maintain all prerequisites of PMOS 5811. c. Requirements. Complete the Special Reaction Team Course (Phase I) (A16MRX3), U.S. Army Military Police School, Ft Leonard Wood, MO or completion of the Marine Corps Police Academy (MCPA) SRT Phase I Training. d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (ac), Military Police, Investigations, and Corrections Training and Readiness Manual.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
